title: The Non-living Environment
seo_title: Primary 1 Basic Science: The Non-living Environment Worksheets (NERDC)
standard_code: Primary 1 Basic Science: Learning About Our Environment
standard_text: The environment has non-living parts: air, water, soil and rocks. Living things depend on them. People use air, water and soil and must keep them clean. (summary of the Basic Science curriculum, Primary 1, theme: Learning About Our Environment)
meta_desc: Free Primary 1 Basic Science worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: Learning About Our Environment): air around us, water in our lives, soil, kinds of soil and rocks. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Air, water, soil and rocks are non-living parts of the environment.
key_sub: Living things need clean air, water and soil.
body_html:
How to think about it

The environment has living parts (plants and animals) and non-living parts (air, water, soil and rocks). Air is all around us; we cannot see it, but we feel it as wind.

Water is in rivers, lakes, seas and rain. Soil is made of tiny bits of rock, dead plants and animals, water and air; plants grow in it. We must keep air, water and soil clean because living things need them.

Example

Is soil living or non-living?

It has living things in it, but it does not grow.

Answer: non-living (with living things in it)

Example

How do you know air is there?

Think of a flag.

Answer: you can feel wind and see things move

Common mistakes

  • Thinking air has no weight or takes up no space.
  • Thinking soil is only dirt with nothing in it.
  • Thinking all water is safe to drink.

faq.q: Why is clay soil good for making pots?
faq.a: It is sticky and holds its shape when wet.

faq.q: How can we keep rivers clean?
faq.a: Do not throw rubbish or waste into rivers and canals.

items.q: Zainab looks outside. A rainbow appears after a shower. What does this tell Zainab?
c: the sun came out after rain
items.e: Clues tell us about the weather.

items.q: Which one shows that the wind is blowing?
items.e: We see what wind moves.

items.q: Gbenga reads: “A cold front catches up to a warm front and lifts the warm air off the ground.” What kind of front is this?
items.e: That describes an occluded front.

items.q: Can we see air?
c: No, because there is no air.
No, but we can feel it move as wind.
items.e: Air is all around us.

items.q: Hauwa looks outside. People wear sunglasses and there are no clouds. What does this tell Hauwa?
items.e: Clues tell us about the weather.

items.q: Which one uses wind to work?
items.e: Wind pushes the sail.

items.q: What is wind?
items.e: Wind can be gentle or strong.

items.q: Which tool shows which way the wind blows?
c: a wind sock or weather vane
items.e: It points with the wind.

items.q: Chiamaka looks out the window. What is the weather?
items.e: The picture shows cloudy weather.

items.q: Dayo looks out the window. What is the weather?
items.e: The picture shows windy weather.

items.q: Nkechi's forecast says a cold front is coming. What weather should Nkechi expect?
c: Light, steady rain or drizzle, then warmer and more humid weather.
Thunderstorms or heavy rain, then cooler and drier weather.
Many days of cloudy, wet weather.
items.e: A cold air mass pushes under a warm air mass and forces it up quickly.

items.q: Segun reads: “A cold air mass pushes under a warm air mass and forces it up quickly.” What kind of front is this?
items.e: That describes a cold front.

items.q: Tobi looks outside. There are puddles everywhere and the grass is wet. What does this tell Tobi?
items.e: Clues tell us about the weather.

items.q: Which tool measures how much rain fell?
items.e: It collects rain.

items.q: Kelechi learns that an air mass formed over the Gulf of Mexico. What will it most likely be like?
items.e: Air masses take on the temperature and humidity of where they form: over warm ocean water near the equator.

c: Many days of cloudy, wet weather.
Thunderstorms or heavy rain, then cooler and drier weather.
Light, steady rain or drizzle, then warmer and more humid weather.

items.q: What is water used for at home?
items.e: We use water every day.

items.q: Which of these is a way to save water?
c: leaving the tap running while soaping hands
taking a long bath every day
washing a few clothes in a full machine
watering plants with water used to wash rice
items.e: Saving water means using only what we need.

items.q: Which of these wastes water?
c: washing clothes only when there is a full load
thawing frozen food under a running tap
using a cup to rinse the mouth
items.e: Water is precious; every drop counts.

items.q: Abdullahi looks at rain. Is this water solid or liquid?
c: It is a gas you can see.
items.e: Rain is liquid water.

items.q: What is rain?
items.e: Rain is part of the water cycle.

items.q: Victor asks: What is an iceberg?
c: a big piece of ice floating in the ocean
items.e: It broke off a glacier.

items.q: Uche looks at a river. Is this water solid or liquid?
c: It is a gas you can see.
items.e: A river is liquid water.

items.q: Which of these wastes water?
c: using a pail instead of a hose to wash the car
taking a long bath every day
watering plants with water used to wash rice
items.e: Water is precious; every drop counts.

items.q: What happens to a kite when the wind blows?

items.e: Moving air pushes the kite.

items.e: Most fresh water is ice.

items.q: What makes clouds?

items.e: Clouds are made of water drops.

items.q: Hadiza looks at water deep under the ground. Is this water solid or liquid?

items.e: Water deep under the ground is liquid water.

items.q: Where does a puddle go on a sunny day?

The water goes into the air.
items.e: Water evaporates.

items.q: What happens to a balloon when you let the air out?
items.e: Air takes up space.

items.q: How does Ikenna know hail is solid water?
c: It is solid, so it keeps its own shape.
It is cold, so it is not water.
It is liquid, so it flows.
items.e: Solids keep their shape. Liquids flow.

items.q: Babatunde looks at these pictures. Which one shows liquid water?
items.e: Rain is liquid water.

items.q: Nonso asks: What is a glacier?
c: a huge, slow river of ice on land
items.e: Glaciers are solid water.

items.q: What is composting?
c: turning food scraps and leaves into rich soil with the help of decomposers
items.e: Compost feeds plants.

items.q: Which type of soil feels gritty and lets water drain through quickly?
items.e: Sandy soil drains fast; clay soil holds water; loam is a mixture most plants like.

items.q: Which of these is a natural part of soil: chocolate, glass beads, living things such as worms or paper clips?
items.e: Soil is made of rock pieces, humus, air, water and living things.

items.q: Which of these is a natural part of soil: glass beads, humus (rotting plants and animals), metal coins or paper clips?
items.e: Soil is made of rock pieces, humus, air, water and living things.

items.q: Which item should NOT go in a compost bin?

items.q: Which of these is NOT a natural part of soil: air, living things such as worms, metal coins or tiny pieces of rock?
items.e: Soil is made of rock pieces, humus, air, water and living things.

items.q: What is humus?
c: the dark part of soil made from decaying plants and animals
items.e: Humus gives soil nutrients.

items.q: Which of these is a natural part of soil: humus (rotting plants and animals), metal coins, plastic bottles or sugar?
items.e: Soil is made of rock pieces, humus, air, water and living things.

items.q: Which layer of the ground is the top layer, dark and full of humus, roots and living things?
items.e: Topsoil on top, then subsoil, then bedrock.

items.e: Sandy soil drains fast; clay soil holds water; loam is a mixture most plants like.

items.q: How do earthworms help soil?

items.e: Worms are good for gardens.

items.q: Which of these is a natural part of soil: chocolate, glass beads, sugar or tiny pieces of rock?
items.e: Soil is made of rock pieces, humus, air, water and living things.

items.e: Sandy soil drains fast; clay soil holds water; loam is a mixture most plants like.

items.q: Which soil feels sticky when wet?
items.e: Clay is smooth and sticky.

items.q: Which type of soil feels sticky when wet and holds lots of water?
items.e: Sandy soil drains fast; clay soil holds water; loam is a mixture most plants like.

items.q: Which of these is a natural part of soil: chocolate, metal coins, paper clips or water?
items.e: Soil is made of rock pieces, humus, air, water and living things.

items.q: Which of these is a natural part of soil: glass beads, living things such as worms, paper clips or sugar?
items.e: Soil is made of rock pieces, humus, air, water and living things.

items.q: Which layer of the ground is the solid rock deep underneath?
items.e: Topsoil on top, then subsoil, then bedrock.

items.q: Where do the rock pieces in soil come from?
c: Rocks are slowly broken into tiny pieces by weather, water and plant roots.
items.e: Weathering.
